A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TITA research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fusion experiments, benchmark comparisons, generalization examples, and component ablations in Tables 1–9 and Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds detailed MEF and MFF component-ablation results in Tables 9–12.

M1.justification: The IPA/ISF interaction modules, OAF branches, task-specific objectives, and FAMO optimization remain unchanged. New Appendix A.1 documents the existing OAF implementation without establishing a modified model or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same IVF, MEF, and MFF datasets and retain Harvard medical-fusion and Quickbird pan-sharpening evaluations. The added ablations concern already evaluated tasks and datasets.

E2.justification: Main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Tables 9–10 newly report TE and PA comparisons against IPA on the existing MEF and MFF tasks; v1 reported these module alternatives only for IVF in Table 5.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample counts, task sampling, metrics, batch size, and the 20,000-iteration training budget remain unchanged. The additional tables reuse existing ablation configurations and reporting metrics; no revised evaluation protocol is specified.

E4.justification: Detailed internal-component analysis expands from IVF to all three trained tasks. New Tables 9–10 examine attention and interaction alternatives on MEF/MFF, while Tables 11–12 examine OAF branch removals and dynamic weighting. These extend beyond the whole-component TI/TA/MO ablations already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results retain the same single-value reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 9–12 add substantial component-level results across MEF and MFF, revealing task-dependent rankings and sensitivities. For example, new Table 11 reports MEF MI of 6.2073 for full TITA versus 4.8277 without dynamic weighting. All numerical entries in earlier Tables 1–8 and the dynamic-weight table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, including the attention mechanisms, objectives, FAMO updates, and Token Exchange formulation, are unchanged. Added OAF tensor dimensions explain implementation rather than introduce new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the claims of task-agnostic fusion through shared interaction and task-specific adaptation, competitive performance, and generalization to unseen tasks. The new evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.2 interprets the additional comparisons as demonstrating IeSF/IPA necessity, while B.3 links MFF's reliance on HPF to high-frequency clarity information. These extend the mechanism discussion, although Table 9 shows mixed MEF outcomes rather than uniformly favorable IPA results.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code repository pointer in the abstract. New Appendix A.1 specifies OAF operand and feature dimensions and identifies its hypernetworks as two-layer MLPs, providing implementation information absent from v1.

R1.justification: The same 62 cited references and the same positioning relative to specialized, unified, and general fusion methods are retained. Bibliographic page-reference changes reflect document reflow.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording edits, shortens affiliations, adds contact information and acknowledgements, and expands the appendix with new subsections and updated cross-references. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Four ablation tables are added using the existing presentation style. The original dynamic-weight Table 9 becomes Table 13, Table 8 moves within the appendix, and text/header spacing changes. Existing figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The OAF implementation details, code-access pointer, and MEF/MFF component tables improve reproducibility information and empirical scrutiny. The benefit is qualified by overgeneralized interpretation: Table 9 shows IPA below TE on MEF MI and VIF despite Appendix B.2's overall-degradation claim. These are useful but bounded gains to an otherwise unchanged method and benchmark evaluation.
